announcement.label: Announcement
announcement.useWhen: One launch or piece of news: a headline, a date, and what's new
announcement.avoidWhen: Several pieces of news at once (use newsletter), or a link preview for an article (use og-card)

certificate.label: Certificate
certificate.useWhen: Recognizing someone for finishing or achieving something: who, what, when, and who signs it
certificate.avoidWhen: A ticket or a pass (use ticket), or a letter with paragraphs of text (use letter)

event.label: Event
event.useWhen: An event people can come to: what it is, when and where, and how to register
event.avoidWhen: A ticket someone already has (use ticket), or one speaker's announcement (use speaker)

feedback-request.label: Feedback request
feedback-request.useWhen: Asking someone for their view after something happened (a stay, a purchase, a call), or showing them a review and inviting their reply
feedback-request.avoidWhen: A survey of many questions (link to it from a newsletter), or a review shown as a quote on an image (use quote-card)

invoice.label: Invoice
invoice.useWhen: A bill the reader has to pay: what it's for, how much, and when it's due
invoice.avoidWhen: A payment already made (use receipt), or an estimate before work starts (use quote)

magic-link.label: Magic link
magic-link.useWhen: A one-time link that signs the reader in without a password
magic-link.avoidWhen: A code to type (use sign-in-code), or resetting a password (use password-reset)

newsletter.label: Newsletter
newsletter.useWhen: A regular issue of written news: a subject, a lead, and sections the writer fills in
newsletter.avoidWhen: One announcement (use announcement), or a summary built from data (use digest)

og-card.label: Open Graph card
og-card.useWhen: The picture a link shows when it's shared: an article's or a page's title, with the brand
og-card.avoidWhen: A launch with features and a product picture (use announcement), or an ad (use ad)

order-confirmation.label: Order confirmation
order-confirmation.useWhen: Confirming an order was placed: what's in it, what it costs, and where it's going
order-confirmation.avoidWhen: Proof of a payment for a subscription (use receipt), or an order on its way (use shipping)

password-reset.label: Password reset
password-reset.useWhen: A link to choose a new password, after someone asked to reset theirs
password-reset.avoidWhen: A code to type instead of a link (use sign-in-code), or telling someone their password was changed (use security-alert)

quote.label: Quote
quote.useWhen: An estimate before work starts: what's included, what it costs, and how long the price holds
quote.avoidWhen: A bill to be paid (use invoice), or a full proposal with its approach and terms (use proposal)

receipt.label: Receipt
receipt.useWhen: Proof of a payment already made: what was bought, what it cost, and when it was paid
receipt.avoidWhen: A bill still to be paid (use invoice), or an order that hasn't been charged yet (use order-confirmation)

report.label: Report
report.useWhen: Numbers about a period, told as a story: a year in review, a monthly summary, usage stats
report.avoidWhen: A bill or a receipt (use invoice or receipt), or news and articles (use newsletter)

shipping.label: Shipping
shipping.useWhen: Telling someone their order is on its way: who's carrying it, when it should arrive, and how to track it
shipping.avoidWhen: Confirming an order was placed (use order-confirmation), or one that has arrived (use delivered)

sign-in-code.label: Sign-in code
sign-in-code.useWhen: A one-time code the reader types to sign in or to confirm an action
sign-in-code.avoidWhen: A link to click instead of a code (use magic-link), or resetting a password (use password-reset)

speaker.label: Speaker
speaker.useWhen: Announcing one speaker for an event: who they are, what they'll talk about, and when
speaker.avoidWhen: The whole event (use event), or a quote from someone (use quote-card)

ticket.label: Ticket
ticket.useWhen: A ticket someone holds for an event: who it's for, when and where, and the code to show at the door
ticket.avoidWhen: Inviting people to an event (use event), or a receipt for the ticket's price (use receipt)

verify-email.label: Verify email
verify-email.useWhen: A link that confirms an email address belongs to the person who signed up with it
verify-email.avoidWhen: A code to type (use sign-in-code), or a first hello with next steps (use welcome)

welcome.label: Welcome
welcome.useWhen: The first email after someone signs up: a greeting, a few next steps and one button
welcome.avoidWhen: Confirming an email address (use verify-email), or a series of onboarding emails with different content

#CodePenChallenge: Cubes. The Shape challenge continues!͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ 

View this Challenge on CodePen

This week: #CodePenChallenge:
Cubes

The Shape challenge continues!

Last week, we kicked things off with round shapes. We "rounded" up the Pens from week one in our #CodePenChallenge: Round collection.

This week, we move on to cubes 🧊

Creating cubes in the browser is all about mastery of illusion. Take control of perspective and shadows and you can make the magic of 3D on a flat screen 🧙

This week is a fun chance to work on your CSS shape-building skills, or dig into a 3D JavaScript library like Three.js.

This week's starter template features an ice cube emoji to help inspire a "cool" idea for your Pen. As always, the template is just a jumping off point. Feel free to incorporate the 🧊 in your creation, add more elements, or freeze it out completely and start over from scratch!

💪 Your Challenge: create a Pen that includes cube shapes.

CodePen PRO

CodePen PRO combines a bunch of features that can help any front-end designer or developer at any experience level.

Learn More

To participate: Create a Pen → and tag it codepenchallenge and cpc-cubes. We'll be watching and gathering the Pens into a Collection, and sharing on Twitter and Instagram (Use the #CodePenChallenge tag on Twitter and Instagram as well).

IDEAS!

🌟

This week we move from 2 dimensions to three! Maybe you could exercise your perspective in CSS to create a 3D cube. Or, you can try out creating 3D shapes in JavaScript, using WebGL or building a Three.js scene.

🌟

There's more to cubes than just six square sides. There are variations on the cube that could be fun to play with this week: cuboid shapes are hexahedrons with faces that aren't always squares. And if you want to really push the boundaries of shape, consider the 4 dimensional tesseract!

🌟

Here's a mind-bending idea that can combine the round shapes from week one with this week's cube theme: Spherical Cubes 😳 Solving longstanding mathematical mysteries is probably outside the scope of a CodePen challenge, but you could use front-end tools to explore fitting spheres into cubes, or vice-versa.

RESOURCES!

📖

Learn all about How CSS Perspective Works and how to build a 3D CSS cube from scratch in an in-depth tutorial for CSS-Tricks. Or, check out stunning examples of WebGL cubes: Just Ice and Posing.

📖

Want to go beyond the square cube? Draw inspiration from Pens like Pulsating Tesseract, Rainbow Cuboid Loader, or Pure CSS cuboid jellyfish.

📖

Did that spherical cubes concept pique your interest? Explore Cube Sphere, 3D Sphere to Cube Animation With Virtual Trackball and Infinitely unpack prism for more mindbending cube concepts that test the boundaries of how shapes interact with each other.

Go to Challenge Page

You can adjust your email preferences any time, or instantly opt out of emails of this kind. Need help with anything? Hit up support.

default.html:
#KeelChallenge: Cubes. The Shape challenge continues!͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ 

View this Challenge on Keel

This week: #KeelChallenge:
Cubes

The Shape challenge continues!

Last week, we kicked things off with round shapes. We "rounded" up the Pens from week one in our #KeelChallenge: Round collection.

This week, we move on to cubes 🧊

Creating cubes in the browser is all about mastery of illusion. Take control of perspective and shadows and you can make the magic of 3D on a flat screen 🧙

This week is a fun chance to work on your CSS shape-building skills, or dig into a 3D JavaScript library like Three.js.

This week's starter template features an ice cube emoji to help inspire a "cool" idea for your Pen. As always, the template is just a jumping off point. Feel free to incorporate the 🧊 in your creation, add more elements, or freeze it out completely and start over from scratch!

💪 Your Challenge: create a Pen that includes cube shapes.

Keel PRO

Keel PRO combines a bunch of features that can help any front-end designer or developer at any experience level.

Learn More

To participate: Create a Pen → and tag it keelchallenge and cpc-cubes. We'll be watching and gathering the Pens into a Collection, and sharing on Twitter and Instagram (Use the #KeelChallenge tag on Twitter and Instagram as well).

IDEAS!

🌟

This week we move from 2 dimensions to three! Maybe you could exercise your perspective in CSS to create a 3D cube. Or, you can try out creating 3D shapes in JavaScript, using WebGL or building a Three.js scene.

🌟

There's more to cubes than just six square sides. There are variations on the cube that could be fun to play with this week: cuboid shapes are hexahedrons with faces that aren't always squares. And if you want to really push the boundaries of shape, consider the 4 dimensional tesseract!

🌟

Here's a mind-bending idea that can combine the round shapes from week one with this week's cube theme: Spherical Cubes 😳 Solving longstanding mathematical mysteries is probably outside the scope of a Keel challenge, but you could use front-end tools to explore fitting spheres into cubes, or vice-versa.

RESOURCES!

📖

Learn all about How CSS Perspective Works and how to build a 3D CSS cube from scratch in an in-depth tutorial for CSS-Tricks. Or, check out stunning examples of WebGL cubes: Just Ice and Posing.

📖

Want to go beyond the square cube? Draw inspiration from Pens like Pulsating Tesseract, Rainbow Cuboid Loader, or Pure CSS cuboid jellyfish.

📖

Did that spherical cubes concept pique your interest? Explore Cube Sphere, 3D Sphere to Cube Animation With Virtual Trackball and Infinitely unpack prism for more mindbending cube concepts that test the boundaries of how shapes interact with each other.

Go to Challenge Page

You can adjust your email preferences any time, or instantly opt out of emails of this kind. Need help with anything? Hit up support.

[Keel]

View this Challenge on Keel (https://keel.example/challenges/cubes)

THIS WEEK: #KEELCHALLENGE:
CUBES

The Shape challenge continues!

Last week, we kicked things off with round shapes. We "rounded" up the Pens from week one in our #KeelChallenge: Round (https://keel.example/collection/challenge-round) collection.

This week, we move on to cubes 🧊

Creating cubes in the browser is all about mastery of illusion. Take control of perspective and shadows and you can make the magic of 3D on a flat screen 🧙

This week is a fun chance to work on your CSS shape-building skills, or dig into a 3D JavaScript library like Three.js.

This week's starter template features an ice cube emoji to help inspire a "cool" idea for your Pen. As always, the template is just a jumping off point. Feel free to incorporate the 🧊 in your creation, add more elements, or freeze it out completely and start over from scratch!

💪 Your Challenge: create a Pen that includes cube shapes. (https://keel.example/challenges/cubes/starter)

[A cube puzzle on a yellow background]

KEEL PRO

Keel PRO combines a bunch of features that can help any front-end designer or developer at any experience level.

Learn More (https://keel.example/features/pro)

To participate: Create a Pen → (https://keel.example/pen/new) and tag it keelchallenge (https://keel.example/tag/keelchallenge) and cpc-cubes (https://keel.example/tag/cpc-cubes). We'll be watching and gathering the Pens into a Collection, and sharing on Twitter (https://keel.example/twitter) and Instagram (https://keel.example/instagram) (Use the #KeelChallenge tag on Twitter and Instagram as well).

IDEAS!

🌟

This week we move from 2 dimensions to three! Maybe you could exercise your perspective (https://keel.example/challenges/cubes/perspective) in CSS to create a 3D cube. Or, you can try out creating 3D shapes in JavaScript, using WebGL (https://keel.example/challenges/cubes/webgl) or building a Three.js scene (https://keel.example/challenges/cubes/three-js).

🌟

There's more to cubes than just six square sides. There are variations on the cube that could be fun to play with this week: cuboid shapes (https://keel.example/challenges/cubes/cuboids) are hexahedrons with faces that aren't always squares. And if you want to really push the boundaries of shape, consider the 4 dimensional tesseract! (https://keel.example/challenges/cubes/tesseract)

🌟

Here's a mind-bending idea that can combine the round shapes from week one with this week's cube theme: Spherical Cubes (https://keel.example/challenges/cubes/spherical-cubes) 😳 Solving longstanding mathematical mysteries is probably outside the scope of a Keel challenge, but you could use front-end tools to explore fitting spheres into cubes, or vice-versa.

RESOURCES!

📖

Learn all about How CSS Perspective Works (https://keel.example/challenges/cubes/css-perspective) and how to build a 3D CSS cube from scratch in an in-depth tutorial for CSS-Tricks. Or, check out stunning examples of WebGL cubes: Just Ice (https://keel.example/challenges/cubes/just-ice) and Posing (https://keel.example/challenges/cubes/posing).

📖

Want to go beyond the square cube? Draw inspiration from Pens like Pulsating Tesseract (https://keel.example/challenges/cubes/pulsating-tesseract), Rainbow Cuboid Loader (https://keel.example/challenges/cubes/rainbow-cuboid-loader), or Pure CSS cuboid jellyfish (https://keel.example/challenges/cubes/cuboid-jellyfish).

📖

Did that spherical cubes concept pique your interest? Explore Cube Sphere (https://keel.example/challenges/cubes/cube-sphere), 3D Sphere to Cube Animation With Virtual Trackball (https://keel.example/challenges/cubes/sphere-to-cube) and Infinitely unpack prism (https://keel.example/challenges/cubes/unpack-prism) for more mindbending cube concepts that test the boundaries of how shapes interact with each other.

Go to Challenge Page (https://keel.example/challenges)

You can adjust your email preferences (https://keel.example/settings/notifications) any time, or instantly opt out (https://keel.example/unsubscribe) of emails of this kind. Need help with anything? Hit up support (https://keel.example/support).

#SlowSignalsChallenge: Cubes. The Shape challenge continues!͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ 

View this Challenge on Slow Signals

This week: #SlowSignalsChallenge:
Cubes

The Shape challenge continues!

Last week, we kicked things off with round shapes. We "rounded" up the Pens from week one in our #SlowSignalsChallenge: Round collection.

This week, we move on to cubes 🧊

Creating cubes in the browser is all about mastery of illusion. Take control of perspective and shadows and you can make the magic of 3D on a flat screen 🧙

This week is a fun chance to work on your CSS shape-building skills, or dig into a 3D JavaScript library like Three.js.

This week's starter template features an ice cube emoji to help inspire a "cool" idea for your Pen. As always, the template is just a jumping off point. Feel free to incorporate the 🧊 in your creation, add more elements, or freeze it out completely and start over from scratch!

💪 Your Challenge: create a Pen that includes cube shapes.

Slow Signals PRO

Slow Signals PRO combines a bunch of features that can help any front-end designer or developer at any experience level.

Learn More

To participate: Create a Pen → and tag it slowsignalschallenge and cpc-cubes. We'll be watching and gathering the Pens into a Collection, and sharing on Twitter and Instagram (Use the #SlowSignalsChallenge tag on Twitter and Instagram as well).

IDEAS!

🌟

This week we move from 2 dimensions to three! Maybe you could exercise your perspective in CSS to create a 3D cube. Or, you can try out creating 3D shapes in JavaScript, using WebGL or building a Three.js scene.

🌟

There's more to cubes than just six square sides. There are variations on the cube that could be fun to play with this week: cuboid shapes are hexahedrons with faces that aren't always squares. And if you want to really push the boundaries of shape, consider the 4 dimensional tesseract!

🌟

Here's a mind-bending idea that can combine the round shapes from week one with this week's cube theme: Spherical Cubes 😳 Solving longstanding mathematical mysteries is probably outside the scope of a Slow Signals challenge, but you could use front-end tools to explore fitting spheres into cubes, or vice-versa.

RESOURCES!

📖

Learn all about How CSS Perspective Works and how to build a 3D CSS cube from scratch in an in-depth tutorial for CSS-Tricks. Or, check out stunning examples of WebGL cubes: Just Ice and Posing.

📖

Want to go beyond the square cube? Draw inspiration from Pens like Pulsating Tesseract, Rainbow Cuboid Loader, or Pure CSS cuboid jellyfish.

📖

Did that spherical cubes concept pique your interest? Explore Cube Sphere, 3D Sphere to Cube Animation With Virtual Trackball and Infinitely unpack prism for more mindbending cube concepts that test the boundaries of how shapes interact with each other.

Go to Challenge Page

    </Email>
  );

templates.code:
// papermark/emails/report.tsx, from hyperelements.dev/templates. Render it with render(<PapermarkReport />) from
// "@hyper-elements/react"; your brand goes in ./brand.ts.

// Ported from React Email's community templates (https://github.com/resend/react-email), MIT License, Copyright 2024
// Plus Five Five, Inc: see _licenses/react-email.txt.
import { Button, Column, Divider, Email, Heading, Image, LineBreak, Link, Row, Section, Text, token } from "@hyper-elements/react";
import { brand } from "./brand";

export const meta = {
  label: "Year in review",
  description: "A year's numbers told as a story: big figures in rounded panels, the reader's activity side by side, where readers were, and a button to share it",
  recreates: { what: "Year in review email", original: "https://github.com/resend/react-email/blob/canary/apps/demo/emails/Community/notifications/papermark-year-in-review.tsx" },
};

const locations = ["United States", "United Kingdom", "Germany", "Japan"];

export default function PapermarkReport() {
  const site = brand.links.site;
  const panel = { padding: token("spacing.xl"), backgroundColor: token("colors.surface"), borderRadius: token("radii.md"), mobile: { padding: [token("spacing.xl"), token("spacing.md")] } } as const;
  const note = { fontSize: token("fontSizes.small"), lineHeight: "20px" } as const;
  const label = { fontSize: token("fontSizes.small"), textTransform: "uppercase", letterSpacing: 0.7 } as const;
  const rule = { borderTop: { width: 1, style: "solid", color: token("colors.accent") }, padding: [token("spacing.lg"), 0, 0] } as const;
  const huge = { fontSize: 72, fontWeight: 700, lineHeight: 1, padding: [token("spacing.md"), 0], mobile: { fontSize: 56 } } as const;
  const button = {
    alignSelf: "center",
    backgroundColor: token("colors.primary"),
    color: token("colors.primaryForeground"),
    fontSize: token("fontSizes.small"),
    fontWeight: 700,
    lineHeight: "20px",
    padding: [token("spacing.md"), 48],
    borderRadius: token("radii.sm"),
  } as const;
  const stat = (what: string, count: number, unit: string) => (
    <Column style={{ width: "33.33%" }}>
      <Text style={{ fontSize: token("fontSizes.small"), color: token("colors.muted") }}>{what}</Text>
      <Text style={{ fontSize: 36, fontWeight: 700, lineHeight: 1.1, padding: [token("spacing.xs"), 0] }}>{count}</Text>
      <Text style={{ fontSize: 24, lineHeight: 1.3, mobile: { fontSize: 18 } }}>{unit}</Text>
    </Column>
  );
  return (
    <Email
      width={600}
      title={`Your Year with ${brand.name}`}
      previewText="See your stats from 2024"
      lang={brand.lang ?? "en"}
      dir={brand.dir}
      theme={brand.theme}
      fonts={brand.fonts}
      style={{
        backgroundColor: token("colors.background"),
        color: token("colors.foreground"),
        fontSize: token("fontSizes.body"),
        lineHeight: token("lineHeights.body"),
        textAlign: "center",
        gap: token("spacing.lg"),
      }}
    >
      <Section>
        <Column style={{ padding: [48, token("spacing.xl"), token("spacing.xl")], alignItems: "center", mobile: { padding: [token("spacing.xl"), token("spacing.md")] } }}>
          <Image src={{ src: brand.logo.src, width: brand.logo.width, height: brand.logo.height }} alt={brand.logo.alt} style={{ width: 122, alignSelf: "center" }} />
          <Text style={{ ...label, padding: [token("spacing.xl"), 0, 0] }}>2024 in review</Text>
          <Heading level={1} style={{ padding: [token("spacing.md"), 0] }}>
            Your Year with {brand.name}
          </Heading>
          <Text style={{ fontSize: 18, lineHeight: "32px", padding: [0, 0, token("spacing.xl")] }}>
            What a year it's been! Let's take a look at how you've used {brand.name} to share your important documents.
          </Text>
          <Button href={`${site}/year-in-review`} style={button}>
            Share your stats
          </Button>
        </Column>
      </Section>

      <Section>
        <Column style={panel}>
          <Heading level={2} style={{ color: token("colors.muted") }}>
            Viewers spent
          </Heading>
          <Text style={huge}>1234</Text>
          <Text style={{ fontSize: 30, lineHeight: 1.2, padding: [0, 0, token("spacing.md")] }}>minutes on your documents</Text>
          <Text style={note}>That's a lot of engagement! Your documents are resonating with your visitors.</Text>
          <Divider style={rule} />
          <Heading level={3} style={{ ...label, padding: [20, 0, 0] }}>
            Your activity
          </Heading>
          <Row stackOnMobile={false} style={{ padding: [20, 0, 0] }}>
            {stat("You uploaded", 25, "documents")}
            {stat("You shared", 50, "links")}
            {stat("You received", 500, "views")}
          </Row>
        </Column>
      </Section>

      <Section>
        <Column style={panel}>
          <Heading level={2}>Your top document</Heading>
          <Text style={{ fontSize: 24, fontWeight: 700, lineHeight: 1.2, padding: [token("spacing.md"), 0] }}>"Q4 Financial Report"</Text>
          <Text style={{ fontSize: 48, lineHeight: 1, padding: [0, 0, token("spacing.md")], mobile: { fontSize: 40 } }}>150 views</Text>
          <Text style={note}>This document really caught your visitor's attention!</Text>
        </Column>
      </Section>

      <Section>
        <Column style={panel}>
          <Heading level={2} style={{ color: token("colors.muted") }}>
            Your most active month
          </Heading>
          <Text style={{ fontSize: 48, fontWeight: 700, lineHeight: 1, padding: [token("spacing.md"), 0], mobile: { fontSize: 40 } }}>September</Text>
          <Text style={{ fontSize: 30, lineHeight: 1.2, padding: [0, 0, token("spacing.md")] }}>with 200 views</Text>
          <Text style={note}>September was your busiest month. What did you share that got so much attention?</Text>
          <Divider style={rule} />
          <Heading level={3} style={{ ...label, padding: [20, 0, 0] }}>
            You're in the top
          </Heading>
          <Text style={huge}>95%</Text>
          <Text style={{ fontSize: 20, lineHeight: 1.4, padding: [0, 0, token("spacing.md")] }}>of sharers on {brand.name}</Text>
          <Text style={note}>You're one of our most active users. Thank you for sharing with {brand.name}!</Text>
        </Column>
      </Section>

      <Section>
        <Column style={panel}>
          <Heading level={2} style={{ color: token("colors.muted") }}>
            Your documents were viewed from
          </Heading>
          <Row stackOnMobile={false} style={{ flexWrap: "wrap", justifyContent: "center", padding: [token("spacing.sm"), 0] }}>
            {locations.map((location) => (
              <Column key={location} style={{ flex: "none", padding: token("spacing.xs") }}>
                <Text
                  style={{
                    fontSize: token("fontSizes.small"),
                    lineHeight: "20px",
                    padding: [token("spacing.xs"), 12],
                    backgroundColor: token("colors.primary"),
                    color: token("colors.primaryForeground"),
                    borderRadius: token("radii.sm"),
                  }}
                >
                  {location}
                </Text>
              </Column>
            ))}
          </Row>
          <Text style={{ ...note, color: token("colors.muted") }}>Your documents get attention from all over the world!</Text>
        </Column>
      </Section>

      <Section>
        <Column style={{ padding: [token("spacing.md"), token("spacing.xl"), token("spacing.lg")], gap: token("spacing.md"), alignItems: "center", mobile: { padding: [token("spacing.md"), token("spacing.md"), token("spacing.lg")] } }}>
          <Text style={{ fontSize: 20, lineHeight: "32px" }}>
            We're excited to support you next year! <LineBreak />
            Happy Holidays from the {brand.name} team :)
          </Text>
          <Button href={`${site}/year-in-review`} style={button}>
            Share your stats
          </Button>
          <Text style={{ fontSize: token("fontSizes.small"), lineHeight: "24px" }}>
            <Link href={`${site}/dashboard`} style={{ color: token("colors.primary"), fontWeight: 700, textDecoration: "none" }}>
              Go to your dashboard
            </Link>
          </Text>
        </Column>
      </Section>
    </Email>
  );
}

Find what you want, faster

Tips and tricks for searching on Stack Overflow

Searching for solutions

With more than 18 million questions, it's possible that someone has already provided a solution to the problem you're facing.

 

Use the search bar at the top of the page to find what you need

Here are a few simple search tips to get you started:

•
To find a specific phrase, enter it in quotes: "local storage"
•
To search within specific tag(s), enter them in square brackets: [javascript]
•
Combine them to get even more precise results - [javascript] "local storage" searches for the phrase “local storage” in questions that have the [javascript] tag

The more information you can put in the search bar, the more likely you will be to either find the answer you need or feel confident that no one else has asked the question before.

Find what you want, faster

Tips and tricks for searching on Slow Signals

Searching for solutions

With more than 18 million questions, it's possible that someone has already provided a solution to the problem you're facing.

 

Use the search bar at the top of the page to find what you need

Here are a few simple search tips to get you started:

•
To find a specific phrase, enter it in quotes: "local storage"
•
To search within specific tag(s), enter them in square brackets: [javascript]
•
Combine them to get even more precise results - [javascript] "local storage" searches for the phrase “local storage” in questions that have the [javascript] tag

The more information you can put in the search bar, the more likely you will be to either find the answer you need or feel confident that no one else has asked the question before.

If you haven't finished your integration, you might find our docs handy.

Once you're ready to start accepting payments, you'll just need to use your live API keys instead of your test API keys. Your account can simultaneously be used for both test and live requests, so you can continue testing while accepting live payments. Check out our tutorial about account basics.

Finally, we've put together a quick checklist to ensure your website conforms to card network standards.

We'll be here to help you with any step along the way. You can find answers to most questions and get in touch with us on our support site.

— The Stripe team

// summit/emails/event.tsx, from hyperelements.dev/templates. Render it with render(<SummitEvent />) from
// "@hyper-elements/react"; your brand goes in ./brand.ts.

import { Button, Column, Email, Heading, Image, Link, Row, Section, Text, token } from "@hyper-elements/react";
import { brand } from "./brand";

export const meta = {
  label: "Event invitation",
  description: "An invitation: the event's name on a band of the brand's color, when and where, a button to register, and the day's schedule",
};

export default function SummitEvent() {
  return (
    <Email
      width={600}
      title="You're invited to Build Day"
      previewText="Thursday, May 14, The Foundry. A day of talks and workshops for the people who build and ship software."
      lang={brand.lang ?? "en"}
      dir={brand.dir}
      theme={brand.theme}
      fonts={brand.fonts}
      style={{ fontSize: token("fontSizes.body"), lineHeight: token("lineHeights.body") }}
    >
      <Section style={{ padding: [token("spacing.lg"), token("spacing.xl")] }}>
        <Image
          src={{ src: brand.logo.src, width: brand.logo.width, height: brand.logo.height }}
          alt={brand.logo.alt}
          style={{ width: 140 }}
        />
      </Section>
      <Section
        style={{
          backgroundColor: token("colors.primary"),
          color: token("colors.primaryForeground"),
          padding: [token("spacing.xl"), token("spacing.xl")],
        }}
      >
        <Column style={{ gap: token("spacing.sm") }}>
          <Text
            style={{
              fontSize: token("fontSizes.small"),
              fontWeight: 700,
              letterSpacing: 1.5,
              textTransform: "uppercase",
            }}
          >
            You're invited
          </Text>
          <Heading level={1} style={{ color: token("colors.primaryForeground") }}>Build Day</Heading>
          <Text>A day of talks and workshops for the people who build and ship software.</Text>
        </Column>
      </Section>
      <Section style={{ padding: [token("spacing.xl"), token("spacing.xl"), token("spacing.lg")] }}>
        <Column style={{ gap: token("spacing.lg") }}>
          <Row stackOnMobile={false} style={{ gap: token("spacing.md"), alignItems: "center" }}>
            <Column style={{ width: 76 }}>
              <Column
                style={{
                  width: 76,
                  backgroundColor: token("colors.surface"),
                  borderRadius: token("radii.md"),
                  padding: [10, 0],
                }}
              >
                <Text
                  style={{
                    fontSize: token("fontSizes.small"),
                    fontWeight: 700,
                    letterSpacing: 1.5,
                    textTransform: "uppercase",
                    color: token("colors.primary"),
                    textAlign: "center",
                  }}
                >
                  May
                </Text>
                <Text style={{ fontSize: 30, fontWeight: 700, lineHeight: 1.1, textAlign: "center" }}>14</Text>
              </Column>
            </Column>
            <Column style={{ gap: 2 }}>
              <Text style={{ fontWeight: 700 }}>Thursday, May 14</Text>
              <Text style={{ color: token("colors.muted") }}>9:30 AM to 6:00 PM</Text>
              <Text style={{ color: token("colors.muted") }}>The Foundry, 120 Mill Street, Pittsburgh</Text>
            </Column>
          </Row>
          <Button
            href={`${brand.links.site}/events/build-day`}
            style={{ borderRadius: token("radii.sm"), padding: [token("spacing.sm"), token("spacing.lg")] }}
          >
            Register for Build Day
          </Button>
        </Column>
      </Section>
      <Section style={{ padding: [0, token("spacing.xl"), token("spacing.xl")] }}>
        <Column
          style={{
            gap: token("spacing.sm"),
            border: { top: { width: 1, style: "solid", color: token("colors.border") } },
            padding: [token("spacing.lg"), 0, 0],
          }}
        >
          <Heading level={2}>The day</Heading>
          <Row stackOnMobile={false} style={{ gap: token("spacing.md") }}>
            <Column style={{ width: 96 }}>
              <Text style={{ fontWeight: 700, color: token("colors.primary") }}>9:30 AM</Text>
            </Column>
            <Column>
              <Text>Doors open, coffee and breakfast</Text>
            </Column>
          </Row>
          <Row stackOnMobile={false} style={{ gap: token("spacing.md") }}>
            <Column style={{ width: 96 }}>
              <Text style={{ fontWeight: 700, color: token("colors.primary") }}>10:00 AM</Text>
            </Column>
            <Column>
              <Text>Opening talk: shipping weekly without breaking anything</Text>
            </Column>
          </Row>
          <Row stackOnMobile={false} style={{ gap: token("spacing.md") }}>
            <Column style={{ width: 96 }}>
              <Text style={{ fontWeight: 700, color: token("colors.primary") }}>1:00 PM</Text>
            </Column>
            <Column>
              <Text>Workshops, in four rooms</Text>
            </Column>
          </Row>
          <Row stackOnMobile={false} style={{ gap: token("spacing.md") }}>
            <Column style={{ width: 96 }}>
              <Text style={{ fontWeight: 700, color: token("colors.primary") }}>5:00 PM</Text>
            </Column>
            <Column>
              <Text>Closing panel, then drinks on the roof</Text>
            </Column>
          </Row>
        </Column>
      </Section>
      <Section
        style={{
          backgroundColor: token("colors.surface"),
          padding: [token("spacing.lg"), token("spacing.xl")],
        }}
      >
        <Text style={{ fontSize: token("fontSizes.small"), color: token("colors.muted") }}>
          {brand.name} · {brand.address}{" · "}
          <Link href={`${brand.links.site}/unsubscribe`}>Stop event invitations</Link>
        </Text>
      </Section>
    </Email>
  );
}
